evidence: src/domain/Catalog.ts: getAvailableStock is the single stock-availability computation, reused by canReserve and reserve.
src/domain/Order.ts: stateOrder, canTransitionTo and canCancelOrder keep the lifecycle and cancellation rules in one place.
src/domain/OrderRepository.ts: save, getById, getByState and getAll only store and query orders, and it imports Order and OrderState from './Order'.
src/domain/Product.ts: a plain Product interface that Catalog uses.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files serve one concern: the order-fulfilment domain model. Product is the shared entity. Catalog holds product and stock/reservation rules. Order holds the order shape and its lifecycle rules. OrderRepository is the order store. Each invariant sits in one place within the unit. Stock availability is computed only in Catalog.getAvailableStock, and canReserve and reserve both use it. The order state sequence and the cancellation rule are defined once in Order.ts (stateOrder, canTransitionTo, canCancelOrder). OrderRepository only stores and queries orders and holds no business rules. No file in the unit bypasses another's abstractions: Catalog uses Product, and OrderRepository uses Order and OrderState. Mixing a class (Catalog) with data types plus functions (Order) is a style difference, not a split in concern or a duplicated rule. I can't see how the application layer uses these, so I can't judge any duplication outside the unit.
